subject: Scalar Invariance Test. LRT error "some models but not all have a mean structure"

messages.author: a42cf44420994080
messages.subject: Scalar Invariance Test. LRT error "some models but not all have a mean structure"
parts:
Dear Lavaan community,

i have an issue with the likelihood ratio test under the call of anova(model1,model2).

I am doing invariance testing and want to test if the metric and the scalar invariance model differ significantly. A few weeks ago this worked well, but now i get the following error message:

anova(modell_2.mi, modell_2.si) 
Error in lavTestLRT(object = object, ..., model.names = NAMES) :
  lavaan ERROR: some models (but not all) have a meanstructure
In addition: Warning message:
In lavTestLRT(object = object, ..., model.names = NAMES) :
  lavaan WARNING: not all models have a meanstructure

both models were estimated using the following commads:

Messmodell_2.si <- sem(modell_2.SCALAR, data = data, missing='listwise', estimator='MLR')

Messmodell_2.mi <- sem(modell_2.METRIC, data = data, missing='listwise', estimator='MLR')

Can anyone help me out?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Scalar Invariance Test. LRT error "some models but not all have a mean structure"
parts:
Do you have a meanstructure in both models? If not, either add
means/intercepts to the model syntax, or add the meanstructure = TRUE
argument to the sem() call.

Yves.

messages.author: a42cf44420994080
messages.subject: Re: Scalar Invariance Test. LRT error "some models but not all have a mean structure"
parts:
I tried the following things

– estimate only the intercepts of the items freely in the metric invariance model by explicitly relaxing the constraints  and then compare the two models
– estimate the intercepts of the items and the LV freely in the metric invariance model by explicitly relaxing the constraints and then compare the two models

both approaches resulted in the same error message.

adding meanstructure = TRUE to the metric invariance model and comparing the metric and the scalar invariance model resulted in the desired outcome.

Maybe it has something to do how Lavaan classifies models as having a mean structure or not: https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/src/R/lav_test_LRT.R

Thanks alot for the help! 

Best, 

Justin
